**Test image observations:**
- Ground-level view of soybean field showing multiple dead/dying plants
- Dark brown to black rotted tissue at the stem base/crown near soil line
- Stems are desiccated, tan-to-brown, plants appear to have wilted and died from the base up
- No visible white mycelium or sclerotia
- "Field death" pattern with multiple plants affected in a cluster

**Candidate analysis:**
- **White Mold**: Reference shows white cottony mycelium and bleached stems — no white fluffy growth visible here
- **Charcoal Rot**: Shows bleached/gray stems with dark internal microsclerotia — stems here are darker brown/black at base
- **Phytophthora**: Reference (lower-left panel) shows multiple dead plants with brown dried stems and dark rotted tissue at the crown, very closely matching the test image pattern — chocolate brown stem lesion extending from soil line upward, multiple plants dying in patches

The Phytophthora reference image lower-left panel is nearly identical to the test image: dead/wilted plants clustered at soil level with brown-black crown/stem rot and dried brown aerial tissue.
